name: express-ejs-inventory
title: Depot Ninety – warehouse inventory (Express 4 + EJS)
description: Classic server-rendered multi-page app for a fictional warehouse: item CRUD with search/filters, a low-stock admin report, express-session cookies, hand-rolled CSRF tokens and a lowdb JSON store.

env.name: SESSION_SECRET
env.description: Secret that signs the express-session cookie. Falls back to the demo value (with a startup warning) when unset; set a long random string in real deployments.

env.name: COOKIE_SECURE
env.description: Set "true" behind HTTPS so the session cookie gets the Secure flag (keep false for plain-HTTP smoke tests).

env.name: TRUST_PROXY
env.description: Set "true" behind a reverse proxy (Express trust proxy = 1).

env.name: DATA_DIR
env.description: Directory holding inventory.json (auto-created and seeded on first start).

auth.description: express-session (in-memory MemoryStore) with cookie `depot.sid`; passwords are bcryptjs hashes. Every state-changing POST must carry the `_csrf` field that matches the token stored in the session (scrape it from any rendered form, e.g. the login page). Unauthenticated page requests are redirected 302 to /login; /admin and item deletion require role admin (403 otherwise).

persistence: lowdb JSON file at data/inventory.json (DATA_DIR), auto-created and seeded with 2 users, 3 categories and 15 items on first start. Sessions live in process memory and are lost on restart.
notes: Needs a writable DATA_DIR (Docker: mount a volume at /app/data). Single-process only (MemoryStore); express-session prints a MemoryStore warning in production - expected for this demo. Tailwind is loaded from cdn.tailwindcss.com in the browser, so end users need internet access for styling (the server itself makes no outbound calls). Smoke test: GET /login with a cookie jar, scrape `name="_csrf" value="..."`, POST /login (form-urlencoded: _csrf, username, password) -> 302 to /items, then GET /items -> 200; GET /admin as clerk -> 403, as admin -> 200. `npm audit` reports 2 moderate advisories in Express 4's transitive `qs`; the fix would be Express 5.
